producer_report.summary: Added `check_speed_timeline`, a reading-gate check, so a reading of a speed or delay request is refused unless it carries a measured stage timeline. Root cause: the reading stage checked a request's own figures only if the reader chose to, so jobs 20261025-110525-8hzb, 20261025-034733-c453 and 20261025-190606-eebk were planned around stated timings with no timeline from the code. The check is one `step!` line in `refusing_check` right after `check_outcome_state`. A speed request is found by whole-word cues and duration targets. Examples are `faster`, `speed up`, `head start`, `takes longer`, and a cut verb with a duration such as `save 12 minutes`. Hestia's slowdown and throughput requests count by their marker line, and a spec request counts exactly when its priority is high. Text other people wrote is never scanned: the prevention lines of a root-cause request, a spec request's requirement statement, and the copied source of an approved-proposal request. Bare `delay`, `timing` or `slow` and settings such as a retry timeout are not cues. A speed request needs a `Timeline:` assumption that names a crates/ path, lists at least two stages each with a duration (or says `no recorded timing`), and says which stage the delay sits in. The reader brief got a seventh rule line. The refusal text gives the form to write. The check judges the shape of the timeline, not whether its figures are true. Fmt, clippy and the full test run pass; the only failures were fixed along the way (see mistakes). Deviation from the plan: I counted request records instead of running a replay, so the refusal share is estimated, not measured (see open_issues).

open_issues: The newly refused share was not measured by a replay. I ran no replay or `athena check-reading` over the stored readings; the `athena status --snapshot` run only gave job counts. Instead I counted request records in the evidence snapshot: 20 of about 1050 jobs hold a strong cue (faster, quicker, speedup, latency, speed up, head start, takes longer, takes too long, too slow), about 2%. That is an upper-bound style estimate, not a measurement. The figure cues and the quoted-text rules were not applied in the count. D163 and the changelog say the 5% is an estimate and name the replay on the real repository as the follow-up.
The check judges the shape of the timeline, not whether its figures are true, so a reader can write invented numbers. This is stated in the doc comment and D163.
A target repository with no crates/ directory cannot meet the crates/ path rule. This is stated in D163.

Quoted text is skipped only for the root-cause, spec-gap and approved-proposal builders. The request that applies a defaults proposal (`accept_request`), the blind-spot request and the failed-job titles of a design review are scanned whole, so a stray cue there would need a Timeline. D163 states this limit.

The corpus shapes for Hestia, spec and approved-proposal requests mirror the builders' line shapes by hand; the unit tests in hestia.rs and work_decisions.rs feed the real builder output through the same detector.
mistakes: My first docs for `check_speed_timeline` had a bare `///` line between paragraphs, which would have failed the declared-intended doc test; I merged it into one paragraph before running the test.
My first draft of `timeline_problem` held a leftover scratch block building a throwaway `entries` list; I removed it before compiling.
D163 first said 'amends D161', which the decision backtest flagged as an unconfirmed link; I reworded it and the changelog line.
The D163 needle in my test was lower case while the text starts 'Prompt-only guidance'; I compared in lower case instead.
I ran a broad file-listing Glob over the evidence records that printed 100 paths I did not need.
learnings: `cargo test` stops at the first failing test binary; use `--no-fail-fast` to see every failure in one run.

crates/athena-cli/tests/backtest.rs treats the words 'amends', 'supersedes' and 'superseded by' followed by a decision id in docs/decisions.md as links that must be in the confirmed list. A new decision should avoid them unless it adds a confirmed link.
A corpus helper that builds a Vec with `Vec::new()` then pushes trips clippy's vec_init_then_push; start the vec with the first case.
The corpus doc-comment test requires the check's `///` paragraph to be one paragraph with no bare `///` line.

The fake reader's reading reaches the real gate in fixture repositories that have no crates/ directory, so a crates/ path in its text must sit in a sentence with an absence phrase to pass `check_reading_references`.
The evidence snapshot holds about 1050 jobs and 898 reading records; Grep over `request.json` works for counting cue words.
desires: A tool that runs the replay of the stored accepted readings against the base and candidate builds from inside the producer's snapshot, to measure the refused share instead of estimating it.
A glob or count mode that reports only a number of matching files without listing paths.
